 Q uestion : Auwe! I was unable to renew my driver’s license, despite having made an appointment months ago, because the DMV’s new computer system couldn’t call up my REAL ID information. I have had the starred license for years and renewed it once before with no trouble and I wasn’t trying to change anything — same name and address. People need to know about this. Bring your documents if you are trying to renew your license, even if you already have the star.
 Answer : It sounds like you fell into a temporary gap that occurred as digital records migrated from the old licensing system to the new one, which the Honolulu Department of Customer Services’ Division of Motor Vehicles launched on Oahu last week. While not all REAL ID data had been transferred by the time the new system went live, virtually all Oahu records were transferred as of Thursday afternoon, so, moving forward, far fewer residents should face the problem you had, CSD Director Kimberly M. Hashiro said by telephone Thursday. That said, CSD does want people to bring their REAL ID verification documents to renewal appointments, even if their license or ID already has the star mark.
 Customers like you who had appointments last week or this week but could not renew because your previously submitted REAL ID documents could not be called up on the computer should email complaints@honolulu.gov for help completing the transaction, Hashiro said.
 Even with the data migration virtually finished, CSD wants people renewing their Hawaii driver’s license or state ID to bring in hard copies of their REAL ID documents for this and future renewals, Hashiro said, to ensure seamless service that requires only one visit to the DMV. The documents must be original or certified ones proving the person’s legal name, date of birth, lawful presence in the United States and principal residency in Hawaii. For a U.S. citizen, a valid U.S. passport would fulfill the first three requirements and a valid Hawaii driver’s license and current vehicle registration or title would fulfill the fourth (two documents are required to prove Hawaii residency). For a longer list of acceptable documents for U.S. citizens and for immigrants with permanent legal status, see 808ne.ws/dmvdoc .
 Federal law, which dictates parameters for states issuing federally compliant REAL IDs, requires documents to be submitted every 16 years. However, Hashiro said CSD relies on “best practices” aimed at providing efficient, convenient customer service, which is best achieved if the customer comes prepared with REAL ID documentation at every renewal appointment, in case a problem arises. For example, someone who had moved without informing the DMV of their new Oahu address wouldn’t be able to renew with outdated proof of residency on file, she said.
 Speaking of driver’s license renewal, we’ve said it before and we’ll say it again: People can renew their Hawaii driver’s license or state ID up to six months ahead of its expiration date, with no loss in the duration of the credential. Schedule your renewal appointment at alohaq.honolulu.gov as soon as your renewal window opens, as appointments at Oahu’s satellite city halls and even its driver licensing centers (which have more appointment slots) fill up months in advance.

 An ongoing spike in the renewal cycle that Hashiro said will last through most of 2027 means the former one-month wait for an appointment has stretched to two or three months or more, depending on the facility.
 Mahalo 
 Mahalo to the blessed person who found and turned in my credit card at Costco Iwilei on Wednesday about 1:30 p.m. I thank you for your honesty and integrity. You spared this kupuna some grief. Mahalo! — L.I.
